task.instructions: Using matplotlib, read correlation.csv, which holds a 6x6 correlation matrix with row and column headers in the first column and first row. Draw a heatmap of the correlation values using the 'coolwarm' colormap, with the correlation value printed inside every cell in black text with font size 12, formatted to exactly two decimal places. Label the x-axis 'Variable' and the y-axis 'Variable', rotate the x tick labels by 45 degrees so they do not overlap, and give the figure the title 'Correlation Matrix'. Add a colorbar labeled 'Correlation'. Save the figure to figure.png with a figure size of 8 by 6 inches.

function.arguments:
{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > create_heatmap.py
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Read the correlation matrix
df = pd.read_csv('correlation.csv', index_col=0)

# Create the figure with specified size
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))

# Create the heatmap with 'coolwarm' colormap
im = ax.imshow(df.values, cmap='coolwarm', aspect='auto')

# Set up the tick labels
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(df.columns)))
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(len(df.index)))
ax.set_xticklabels(df.columns)
ax.set_yticklabels(df.index)

# Rotate x tick labels by 45 degrees
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Set axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Variable')
ax.set_ylabel('Variable')

# Set title
ax.set_title('Correlation Matrix')

# Add correlation values inside each cell
for i in range(len(df.index)):
    for j in range(len(df.columns)):
        text = ax.text(j, i, f"{df.values[i, j]:.2f}",
                      ha="center", va="center", color="black", fontsize=12)

# Add colorbar
cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label('Correlation')

# Save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=100, bbox_inches='tight')
print("Figure saved as figure.png")
EOF
"}
